definition: Ritualized means turned into a fixed form repeated the same way each time.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ritualized. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ritualized should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Bedtime at their house is ritualized down to the minute: two books, one song, lights out on the second verse.
Customary is the loosest rung — what is usually done, with plenty of room to vary; a ritualized practice has lost that room, hardening into one fixed form.
Habitual stops short of ritualized: a habitual coffee is automatic for one person, while a ritualized one has hardened into a fixed form someone else could perform in your place.

Formalized means given an official, fixed shape by some authority — a complaint process formalized in the employee handbook. Ritualized form hardens from below instead, out of repetition and shared meaning: nobody legislated the dojo's two bows, yet the sequence is more fixed than any bylaw.

Scripted means following set words or moves that someone wrote and could rewrite tomorrow — a scripted apology has an author to blame. A ritualized practice has no author anyone can point to; its fixed form wore in through repetition, and it resists change because no one owns it.

New students learn the sequence before they learn a single throw, and a visitor who skips it is simply shown the shoe rack and invited to start again.
Ritualized is the right word because the practice has been turned into a fixed form repeated the same way each time — and the form, not the content, carries the meaning.

At the campus radio station, the last shift of the night ends the same way it has since at least the 1980s.
The departing host reads the weather for a town nobody can find on a map, plays thirty seconds of static, and signs off with 'good night, whoever you are.' No manual requires any of it.
Alumni interviewed for the station's anniversary could not say who started it, only that they had inherited it from the host before them.
The sequence has become fully ritualized: hosts who once found it silly admit they cannot bring themselves to change a word.
When the station moved buildings, engineers packed the transmitter last -- so that the sign-off would never once be missed.
